tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on the Harborview demo — rooms show 'unnamed' because PDFTron outlines ALL text (live-text lane finds zero). v2 = opt-in M3 tiles AI lane + callout-vs-room filter.

prep.what: Build an opt-in AI label reading lane for firms that outline all text (making the free lane useless), plus filtering to exclude callouts and notes from being misidentified as room names.
prep.understand: PDFTron-rendered PDFs outline all text as paths, so `live_text` returns 0 results on those firms. The M3 tiles lane runs a vision model on cropped tile images (~4.3 min/sheet, costs credits) to read room labels. A callout filter must then separate real room labels from general-note paragraphs, UP arrows, and FEC callouts — all documented in R13 as known noise.
approach: Review `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` and `engine/labels.py` to understand the M3 tiles spike and where the live-text lane plugs in
Add a `POST /sheets/{id}/labels/ai` opt-in route (or a flag on the existing labels route) that triggers the M3 tiles lane — verify MINIMAX_AI key is present in VPS `.env` before building
Implement the callout-vs-room filter: skip text regions that are single-char/arrows, multi-line paragraph clusters (count > 2 lines), or match FEC/stair callout patterns (R13 documented)
Validate against Holabird (92/109 named, working case) and Harborview demo (0 named, the failing case) — look for improvement without new gauntlet regressions
resources: STATE.md R13 block (callout noise types listed)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: The last pillar between us and estimator-grade Excel. assemblies-lite already folded into B1 (engine/assemblies.py scaffold). Full version = room type → assemblies + formulas + heights (one classification → up to 8 quantities, CSI libraries).

prep.what: Build the full room-type-to-assemblies system: map each room classification to up to 8 trade quantity rows (paint SF, drywall SF, flooring SF, base trim LF) and wire them into the Excel export.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` has a lite scaffold already in place from B1. The full version needs a classification → assembly definition table, formula rules driven by measurement geometry (area/perimeter from the API), and wall_height for vertical surfaces. This is what upgrades the Excel from area-only to fully estimator-grade.
approach: Study `engine/assemblies.py` (the lite scaffold) and the 5-tab Excel output from `engine/excel.py` to map the current data flow

Build the classification → assembly definition table: for each room type (bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, corridor, etc.) define which assemblies apply and which geometry field drives each quantity (area, perimeter, or derived wall SF)
Implement per-room quantity formulas: floor SF = `meta.area`, wall SF = `meta.perimeter × wall_height_ft`, base trim LF = `meta.perimeter`, ceiling SF = `meta.area`
Wire into `build_sheet_takeoff` orchestrator so all quantities flow into the Excel workbook automatically on export; run the gauntlet (85+ checks) and service pytest to confirm no regression
resources: CSI MasterFormat division refs (standard assembly cost codes for validation)
service pytest (run before and after to catch regressions)

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add wall/ceiling height input (project default + per-room override); wall paint SF = perimeter x height. Seeder currently drops geometry — preserve it.

prep.what: Add wall_height_ft to estimates and compute wall paint SF (perimeter × height) per room — fills the zero-SF gap that makes CT Pros painting estimates useless from a takeoff.
prep.understand: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` currently drops `geometry.rings` and `meta.perimeter` from measurement responses. To compute wall area you need to (1) preserve perimeter, (2) add `wall_height_ft` to the estimate model, and (3) derive SF. This also establishes the pattern for t46 to route wall SF to the painting trade.
approach: Create a migration: add `wall_height_ft` (nullable decimal, default 9.0) to the `estimates` table
Update `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` to preserve `meta.perimeter` from each measurement (find where the seeder discards the measurement detail and save it alongside `meta.area`)
Derive wall paint SF per room: `wall_paint_sf = perimeter * wall_height_ft`; emit as a dedicated line item using `LineItemFactory` with a wall_paint kind
Add a wall height input to the Takeoff UI — project-level default in `Takeoff/Index.vue` with optional per-room override in the Review room table
resources: app/Http/Controllers/TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php (the seeder dropping geometry — find and fix the drop)
resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue + TakeoffReview.vue (UI surface for height input)
takeoff-engine /measurements API response schema (perimeter lives in `meta` block)
Rafa: 'I need to know the area of the wall — height × width of the walls'

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' + label, wire LineItemFactory unit, seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing in t46/t48.

prep.what: A tight prerequisite: add `per_linear_ft` to the RateType enum and seed a trim labor rate — the ~30-min schema + seeder change that unblocks t46 from pricing trim/wall-linear measurements.
prep.understand: Without a linear-foot RateType, `LineItemFactory` can't map LF measurements to a unit label or labor rate. This is a pure enum extension + seeder row — no migration needed, no frontend changes required.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with label 'Per Linear Foot'
Add a trim labor rate row in `LaborRateSeeder.php`: trade='trim', crew_type='subcontractor', rate_type=PerLinearFt, a reasonable market rate (e.g. $3.50/lf)

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind+geometry. Switch on kind: area(SF)→flooring, derived wall SF→painting, line(LF)→wall-linear/trim, count(EA)→doors/tile. Tag each with trade via core-vs-subbed helper.

prep.what: Fix the TakeoffEstimateSeeder to route each measurement to its correct trade instead of dumping everything as anonymous custom lines — the change that makes the seeded estimate immediately useful.
prep.understand: The seeder receives a `measurements` array from the engine API. It currently ignores the `kind` field and emits every row as `kind=custom` with $0. The fix adds a switch that maps kind → the right `LineItemFactory` call, using the `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` helper already built in t35/t36. This depends on t45 (for derived wall SF) and t47 (for LF unit type) being done first.
approach: Open `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` and locate the measurement loop where `kind` is currently ignored

Add a switch on measurement `kind`: `area` → flooring (fromMaterial with flooring LaborRate), derived wall SF (from t45) → painting (fromMaterial with painting rate), `line` (LF) → trim (fromLaborRate with PerLinearFt from t47), `count` (EA) → door/fixture
Tag each line with the correct trade via `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` — painting/flooring = own_team, trim = subcontractor per Rafa's business model
Test end-to-end with a painting-type estimate: verify wall lines land under painting trade, no cross-seeds from flooring or framing
resources: app/Http/Controllers/TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php (the seeder to fix — find the measurement loop)
